A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Vivid-VR work, with readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting comparison. v1 ends with references; v3 additionally contains Appendix A, including Tables 3–4 and Figure 8.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative restoration results across six benchmarks, component ablations in Table 2, and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds captioner, connector, training-data, ControlNet-depth and sampling-guidance experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the reported ControlNet depth from N/6 to N/7 blocks and correspondingly revises connector indexing in Equation 1. Appendix A introduces restoration-guided latent updates during inference. These are localized architecture and sampling changes; concept distillation, the projector, dual-branch connector and training loss remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training domains and six evaluation datasets: SPMCS, UDM10, YouHQ40, VideoLQ, UGC50 and AIGC50. v3 corrects the UMD10 table label to UDM10. Added analyses vary configurations and sample counts within retained video-restoration coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all eight external comparators. Table 2 adds skip-connection-plus-cross-attention and Qwen2.5-VL-captioned training variants, and Table 4 adds a one-block ControlNet comparator. Figure 7 removes DOVE from that particular comparison while adding the Qwen variant.

E3.justification: The reported ControlNet size changes from N/6 to N/7. New controlled experiments vary captioning, connector design, generated-video counts, source-video inclusion and ControlNet depth; Figure 8 tests guidance coefficients 1, 5, 10 and 20. The main resolution, training budget, inference-step count and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands tests of the method's design choices. Sections 5.2–5.3 add a convergent skip-connection control and a stronger-captioner alternative. Appendix A tests generated-data volume, generated-only training, one versus N/7 ControlNet blocks, and the fidelity–quality trade-off under sampling guidance. These address questions beyond v1's component-removal ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises full-reference scores and rankings: DOVE's UDM10 PSNR changes from 18.36 to 30.53, moving from last to first, while Vivid-VR's SPMCS PSNR changes from 20.18 to 21.73. No-reference scores remain unchanged. Tables 2–4 and Figure 8 add control, data-volume, depth and guidance findings. The illustrative DOVE LPIPS value also changes from 0.3566 to 0.3112. The PDFs do not explain the causes of the benchmark-score revisions.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds the mathematical definition of restoration-guided sampling in Equation 3, using a time-dependent interpolation toward the input latent. This is a limited formal addition; the training objective remains unchanged and neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contribution statements and conclusion retain the same principal claims: concept distillation mitigates drift, the projector and dual-branch connector improve control, and Vivid-VR performs favorably on synthetic, real-world and AIGC videos. Additional experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v1 states that a more accurate captioner would solve the alignment problem; v3 argues that latent-space discrepancies can persist and interprets the Qwen experiment as support. Appendix A substantially expands qualifications: generative strength can compromise fidelity, additional generated data has diminishing returns, and generated-only training suffers from imperfections in the base model's outputs.

D1.justification: v3 documents sampling guidance and illustrated coefficient values, additional training-data configurations, and same-settings retraining for the one-block control. It also adds a project-homepage pointer for further visual comparisons. The existing repository link, hardware, optimizer, learning rate and training-time disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Deng et al.'s Acquire and Then Adapt to motivate the one-block control, removes the foundational ViT and Attention Is All You Need references, and extends discussion of the already-cited SUPIR to fidelity and sampling guidance. The overall positioning around concept distillation and improved ControlNet remains.

P1.justification: v3 condenses related work, rewrites parts of the concept-distillation motivation and ablation discussion, makes terminology and notation edits, and appends Appendix A. The title, abstract and main Sections 1–6 retain their overall organization.

P2.justification: Visual evidence expands through new Tables 3–4 and the full-page, multi-example guidance comparison in Figure 8. Table 2 expands from six to eight configurations; Figures 6–7 replace comparison panels and revise labels and captions. Figures 1–5 and the general two-column layout remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: The added skip-connection and captioner controls, data-mixture analysis and depth test better justify design choices that v1 supported less directly. Appendix A also makes fidelity limitations and sampling control more explicit. These provide a useful but limited quality gain: substantial Table 1 score revisions and the ControlNet-depth change remain unexplained, limiting confidence in the revised experimental account.
